title: Managing with Style? Micro-Evidence on the Allocation of Managerial Attention
authors: Desmond Lo; Francisco Brahm; Wouter Dessein; Chieko Minami
eligible_reason: No binary staggered treatment. Survey analyses (Tables 3-5) are cross-sectional OLS of managers' attention ratios on log expertise ratios and time-stress measures; the panel 'difference-in-difference' (Table 6, Eq. 2) interacts a continuous log expertise ratio with recurring high-season months, with sales-manager and month FE. Treatment is continuous and the season indicator switches on and off for all units simultaneously.
design_notes: Chile Stata code Panel data - Managing with style.do: xtreg ln_ratio_s lnratio_exp_23to90 hs_lnrat_exp i.period if both_cat==1 & ratio_sales>0.05, fe robust (Table 6 col 5); id_sup x period monthly panel 2015m1-2017m8, 120 sales managers, 1,792 rows. Japan and Chile survey do-files: reg ltimeratio/leffratio on lexp2ratio, time stress, interaction, controls (Tables 3-5).
